name: Dead Bug with Arm/Leg Extension
description: The dead bug with arm and leg extension is a rehabilitation-originated core stability exercise in which the athlete lies supine with the lower back pressed flat, then alternately extends the opposite arm and leg toward the floor while resisting spinal rotation and lumbar extension. Unlike crunches, this exercise trains the core in its primary stabilization function — resisting motion while the limbs create destabilizing forces — making it highly transferable to athletic performance and injury prevention.

execution.starting_position: Lie on your back with the lower back pressed firmly to the floor. Arms extended vertically above the chest, hips and knees at 90 degrees (tabletop position for the legs).
execution.setup_instructions: Use a mat. The key is to feel the lower back pressing into the floor and to maintain this contact throughout the entire movement.
steps: Step 1: Begin in the starting position with arms vertical and legs in tabletop.
Step 2: Take a deep breath and brace the core by pushing the lower back into the floor.
Step 3: Simultaneously lower the right arm overhead toward the floor and extend the left leg, lowering the heel toward the floor.
Step 4: Move slowly and do not let the lower back arch away from the floor.
Step 5: Return to the starting position with control, then repeat on the opposite side.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale forcefully before each rep to engage the core. Breathe continuously but maintain the brace throughout the limb extension.
common_mistakes: Allowing the lower back to arch away from the floor as the limbs extend
Moving too fast — this is a slow, deliberate stability exercise
Extending the leg at the knee rather than lowering the entire leg as a unit
safety_considerations: If the lower back arches, reduce leg extension (do not fully straighten the leg or only lower the leg partway).
Appropriate for most populations including post-partum and those with lower back pain, when performed correctly.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension means the extended leg is nearly parallel to the floor and the arm reaches fully overhead. Reduce range if lower back contact is lost.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 3–4 seconds per limb extension, 2 seconds to return. Slow and deliberate.
coaching_cues: Flatten your back into the floor — no gaps
Move like you are in slow motion
Opposite arm and leg extend together
